reasons: Cited Section 14.1 is symmetric and contains an express M&A/substantially-all-assets carve-out permitting Customer (Corio) to assign without consent, so the walk-away scenario (blanket prohibition with no M&A carve-out) does not apply.

No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists in Section 11 or elsewhere in the cited text, consistent with the rule's requirement that Vendor gain no exit on Customer's change of control; the deterministic check for a successor/affiliate carve-out also passes.

Classification as compliant-at-fallback is correct: mutual successor assignment with symmetric consent for other transfers meets the fallback on material terms, and the shortfalls (no express affiliate carve-out, no 'not unreasonably withheld' qualifier) are properly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed — the rendered text is unchanged from the original paragraphs — and the symmetric direct-competitor proviso is correctly left undisturbed as it also protects our party.
